explanations.explanation: That’s the land they head to. The famine sends them packing, and Moab’s where they settle. (Ruth 1:1)
Egypt’s a famous famine escape, but not this time. This family’s moving to Moab. (Ruth 1:1)
Edom’s not the spot. The text says Moab, and Moab’s where they go. (Ruth 1:1)
Ruth’s the one. She’s the Moabite woman who sticks with Naomi. (Ruth 1:4)
Rachel’s a famous name, but she’s not in this story. Naomi’s sons marry Orpah and Ruth. (Ruth 1:4)
Dinah’s from Genesis, not Ruth. The two Moabite women here are Orpah and Ruth. (Ruth 1:4)
Heartbreak on heartbreak. After ten years in Moab, both Mahlon and Chilion die, and Naomi’s left alone. (Ruth 1:5)

explanations.answer: Her house in Moab burns down
explanations.explanation: No fire here. The text says both of her sons die. (Ruth 1:5)

explanations.answer: She falls sick and loses her sight
explanations.explanation: No sickness, no blindness. The tragedy is the loss of her two sons. (Ruth 1:5)
The LORD’s provided food for His people back in Judah. That’s the news that gets Naomi moving. (Ruth 1:6)
No king mentioned here. The text says the LORD’s given His people food. (Ruth 1:6)
Not victory. The news is about food, and that’s what brings Naomi home. (Ruth 1:6)

explanations.answer: Go back to their mothers' homes
explanations.explanation: Naomi tells them to go back to their mothers’ homes. She’s trying to send them away for their own good. (Ruth 1:8)

explanations.answer: Walk faster to beat the dark
explanations.explanation: No rush here. Naomi’s telling them to go back to their mothers’ homes. (Ruth 1:8)

explanations.answer: Stay close to her the whole way
explanations.explanation: She’s not asking them to stick close. She’s telling them to go back to their mothers’ homes. (Ruth 1:8)
True. Naomi blesses them and says she hopes they each find rest in the home of a new husband. (Ruth 1:9)
It’s true. Naomi’s send-off includes that hope for them. (Ruth 1:9)

explanations.answer: We will return with you to your people
explanations.explanation: They both say they’ll go back with her. That’s their first answer to Naomi’s plea. (Ruth 1:10)

explanations.answer: We will stay in Moab and wait for you
explanations.explanation: No waiting in Moab. They tell Naomi they’ll return with her to her people. (Ruth 1:10)

explanations.answer: We will come visit you in Bethlehem
explanations.explanation: Not just a visit. They say they’ll return with her to her people. (Ruth 1:10)

explanations.answer: Would you wait for them to grow up
explanations.explanation: Naomi asks if they’d wait for sons to grow up. She’s making it clear how hard that road would be. (Ruth 1:13)

explanations.answer: Would you raise them as your own
explanations.explanation: Not raising them. Naomi’s question is whether they’d wait for them to grow up. (Ruth 1:13)

explanations.answer: Would you go ahead to Bethlehem
explanations.explanation: No going ahead. Naomi asks if they’d wait for sons to grow up. (Ruth 1:13)

explanations.answer: The LORD's hand has turned against her
explanations.explanation: Naomi says the hand of the LORD has gone out against her. That’s why she calls it bitter. (Ruth 1:13)

explanations.answer: The people of Judah have turned against her
explanations.explanation: Not the people of Judah. Naomi says it’s the LORD’s hand against her. (Ruth 1:13)

explanations.answer: The people of Moab have turned against her
explanations.explanation: No, it’s not Moab. Naomi says the LORD’s hand has turned against her. (Ruth 1:13)
True. Orpah kisses Naomi goodbye and heads back. (Ruth 1:14)
It’s true. Orpah kisses Naomi goodbye and goes back to her people. (Ruth 1:14)
No, Ruth doesn’t go back with Orpah. She clings to Naomi. (Ruth 1:14)
False. Ruth doesn’t go back home. She clings to Naomi and stays with her. (Ruth 1:14)
True. Naomi tells Ruth to follow Orpah back home after Orpah leaves. (Ruth 1:15)
It’s true. Naomi points out Orpah’s gone and tells Ruth to follow her. (Ruth 1:15)

explanations.answer: Naomi's God will be her God
explanations.explanation: Ruth’s all in. She tells Naomi, "Your God will be my God." That’s the heart of her promise. (Ruth 1:16)

explanations.answer: She will take care of Naomi's house
explanations.explanation: Not about the house. Ruth promises Naomi’s God will be her God. (Ruth 1:16)

explanations.answer: She will learn all the ways of Judah
explanations.explanation: No learning curve here. Ruth’s promise is that Naomi’s God will be her God. (Ruth 1:16)
Ruth swears it: nothing but death separates them. That’s how serious she is. (Ruth 1:17)
Not distance. Ruth says nothing but death separates them. (Ruth 1:17)
No, not marriage. Ruth’s line is clear: nothing but death. (Ruth 1:17)

explanations.answer: She stops trying to persuade her
explanations.explanation: Naomi sees Ruth’s mind is made up, so she stops trying to talk her out of it. (Ruth 1:18)

explanations.answer: She sends her back after Orpah
explanations.explanation: No sending back. Naomi stops trying to persuade her. (Ruth 1:18)

explanations.answer: She tells her to wait in Moab
explanations.explanation: No waiting. Naomi stops trying to persuade her. (Ruth 1:18)
The women of Bethlehem can’t believe their eyes. They say, "Can this be Naomi?" (Ruth 1:19)
Not that. The women exclaim, "Can this be Naomi?" (Ruth 1:19)
No, they recognize her—or think they do. They say, "Can this be Naomi?" (Ruth 1:19)
Naomi tells them to call her Mara. She says the Almighty’s dealt bitterly with her. (Ruth 1:20)
Not Hannah. Naomi says call her Mara. (Ruth 1:20)
No, not Leah. Naomi says call her Mara. (Ruth 1:20)
No, it’s the opposite. Naomi says she went away full and the LORD brought her back empty. (Ruth 1:21)
False. Naomi says she went away full and came back empty. (Ruth 1:21)
They arrive at the beginning of the barley harvest. The timing’s perfect. (Ruth 1:22)
Not wheat. The text says barley harvest. (Ruth 1:22)
No olives here. It’s the barley harvest. (Ruth 1:22)
